tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PolynomialGaloisG.summary: The lower half of this roadmap is largely built, mostly in Tau Ceti's TauCeti/FieldTheory/GaloisGroups/ and TauCeti/GroupTheory/Perm/ (sorry-free): the degree/orbit/stabilizer dictionary, fullCycleType with a full API, the block↔intermediate-field order anti-isomorphism, 2-transitivity, the fibre-product description of Gal(pq), the whole discriminant layer (root-product formula, base change, discr ≠ 0 ↔ separable, δ = discrSqrt, the alternating-group test, the quadratic extension discrField, though without base-field functoriality or the worked cubic instances), factorDegrees with its API, Frobenius orbits over a finite field, general wreath products (without the primitivity theorem for the product action or the comparison with RegularWreathProduct), and the reference subgroups nTj for n ≤ 5. Mathlib contributes more than the roadmap's summary credits: block_stabilizerOrderIso (Wielandt 7.5) is already there, as is the whole Jordan file with the swap and 3-cycle theorems. Two items called absent have their ingredients in the libraries: the conjugate-field dictionary (IsGalois.map_fixingSubgroup, Subgroup.fixedField_map_conj, algHomAdjoinIntegralEquiv) and the root-enumeration facts of Layer 4 (Polynomial.splits_iff_card_roots, nodup_roots_iff_of_splits). Genuinely missing: everything specific to resolvents beyond the universal machinery — there is no ResolventSpec, none of the three registered invariants, no resolventCubic or resolventSextic, no factorization theorem, no Tschirnhaus transform, no quartic decision table and no quintic solvability criterion; Jordan's p-cycle theorem (still a TODO in Mathlib's Jordan.lean) and the imprimitivity wreath embedding; the whole of Layer 6 above the label definitions — HasGaloisLabel, the classification of transitive subgroups for n ≤ 5, and QuinticCertificate; the imported Dedekind statement and the membership statement of Layer 5; and all of Layer 9. Layer 9 has no declaration of any kind in the baseline.

targets.target: Degree bookkeeping: rootSet has natDegree elements, the action is faithful, Nat.card p.Gal = Nat.card of the image
targets.note: Exactly the three Mathlib inputs the layer names, plus the Tau Ceti conclusion and the divisibility of |Gal| by n!.

targets.target: fullCycleType with its full API: simp form, sum, conjugacy invariance, permCongr naturality, comparison with cycleType, count of fixed points
targets.note: Sixteen declarations in Partition.lean cover every bullet the layer lists — constructor, the identity value, the empty-type edge case, conjugacy invariance (fullCycleType_eq_of_isConj, fullCycleType_conj), inverse invariance, and the permCongr transport.

targets.target: Orbits and irreducible factors: the orbit of a root is the root set of its minimal polynomial, and the orbit quotient is in bijection with the distinct monic irreducible factors
targets.note: The bijection, not just the count, and it sends the orbit of α to minpoly F α; the cardinality equality is derived from it, as the layer demands.

targets.target: Transitivity iff irreducibility, for separable p of positive degree
targets.note: The iff carries separability, which the layer says cannot be dropped; Mathlib supplies only the reverse implication.

targets.target: Invariants of the image: order, parity, solvability, cycle types
targets.note: Order and cycle types are there; the parity invariant appears as the alternating-containment side of the Layer 3 discriminant test rather than as a standalone character p.Gal →* ℤˣ, and no declaration packages the sign character itself.

targets.target: Polynomials and normal closures: an explicit MulEquiv f.Gal ≃* Aut(normalClosure(F(α)/F)), with the stabilizer of α the subgroup fixing F(α)
targets.note: Missing: the isomorphism itself. The stabilizer half is proved (stabilizer = fixingSubgroup of F(α), of index natDegree p), and Mathlib has IntermediateField.normalClosure with its IsGalois instance, but no declaration in either library identifies f.Gal with the automorphism group of the normal closure of F(α)/F.

targets.target: Conjugate fields: G/H in equivariant bijection with the roots and with the F-embeddings; conjugate subfields correspond to conjugates of H; their number is [G : N_G(H)]
targets.note: The ingredients are there: conjugate subfields correspond to conjugate subgroups (IsGalois.map_fixingSubgroup in Mathlib, Subgroup.fixedField_map_conj in Tau Ceti, both for general extensions), the F-embeddings of F(α) are in bijection with the roots of its minimal polynomial (IntermediateField.algHomAdjoinIntegralEquiv), G/H ≃ orbit (MulAction.orbitEquivQuotientStabilizer), and the stabilizer's fixed field is F(α). Missing: the three statements assembled for f.Gal, the G-equivariance of the bijections, and the count [G : N_G(H)] of conjugate fields.

duplicates.note: Uses the same fullCycleType invariant on permutations of Fin n (for the three components of a permutation triple), so it consumes this layer's definition rather than restating it.
States Dedekind's theorem using this layer's fullCycleType, and is the declared supplier of the theorem Layer 5 imports.

Its milestone 7.1 builds the same permutation representation for a number field K: the action of Gal(M/ℚ) on the embeddings K →ₐ[ℚ] M, transitive and faithful with card = [K : ℚ], and a permutation embedding into S_n that is canonical only up to conjugacy. That is this layer's embeddings side of the conjugate-field dictionary and its normal-closure setup, specialized to ℚ.

targets.target: The block-stabilizer correspondence: blocks containing a ≅ the interval [stabilizer G a, ⊤], for a transitive action
targets.note: Already in Mathlib in full, cited to the same source (Wielandt Thm 7.5), as {B | a ∈ B ∧ IsBlock G B} ≃o Set.Ici (stabilizer G a) with inverse H ↦ orbit H a, under [IsPretransitive G X]. The roadmap says Mathlib has only 'the two ends' of it; that understates what is there.

targets.target: The two extremal cases: a minimal block gives a primitive stabilizer action on B; a maximal block gives a primitive action on the block system
targets.note: Both directions, in the Mathlib namespace, transported along the order isomorphism above. The iterated chain of imprimitivity is not assembled as a named object, but its two steps are.

targets.target: General wreath products (ι → D) ⋊ Perm ι and (ι → D) ⋊ Q, with constructors, order formulas, functoriality, edge cases, and the two actions
targets.note: Thirty-six declarations, generalizing Mathlib's RegularWreathProduct as planned: both order formulas, map/congr functoriality with composition laws, the empty/singleton/trivial-base edge cases, and both the imprimitive and the product action. Missing from this item: the primitivity theorem for the product action (its hypotheses are stated in the roadmap but no declaration proves it), and the comparison MulEquiv with D ≀ᵣ Q.

targets.target: Imprimitivity gives a wreath embedding: a transitive G with a nontrivial proper block embeds in WreathProduct (Perm B) (block system)
targets.note: Not in either library. WreathProduct.lean stops at the two actions of the wreath product itself; nothing maps a transitive group with a block system into one (Dixon–Mortimer Thm 2.6A).

targets.target: Jordan's theorem for a p-cycle: a primitive subgroup of Sₙ containing a p-cycle with p prime and p + 3 ≤ n contains Aₙ
targets.note: Mathlib's Jordan.lean lists it as a TODO in its module docstring ('Prove Equiv.Perm.alternatingGroup_le_of_isPreprimitive_of_isCycle_mem … Wielandt 13.9') — a comment, not a proof_wanted declaration as the roadmap says — and Tau Ceti has no theorem of that name. Only the 3-cycle case is proved.

targets.target: The recognition theorems: p-cycle in a transitive subgroup of S_p; transposition in prime degree gives S_p; an (n−1)-cycle gives 2-transitivity; a primitive group with a transposition is Sₙ or with a 3-cycle contains Aₙ; an odd power that is a transposition
targets.note: All five are present — the first three and the (n−1)-cycle ⇒ 2-transitive ⇒ primitive chain in Tau Ceti, the last two consumed from Mathlib's Jordan.lean exactly as the layer directs.

duplicates.note: Also works with MulAction.IsBlock and block systems for monodromy groups, and states its label membership 'exactly as PolynomialGaloisGroups spells label membership'; the block theory is shared, not duplicated.

Milestone 1 of its general Evens-norm construction is 'the wreath product itself': the permutation wreath product (X → D) ⋊ Q for a Q-set X, generalizing Mathlib's RegularWreathProduct. That is the same object as this layer's general wreath product, so one construction should serve both.

targets.target: Stabilizers are relative Galois groups: stabilizer p.Gal α = (adjoin F {α}).fixingSubgroup, of index natDegree p
targets.note: Both the fixingSubgroup identity and the index, plus the fixed field of the stabilizer and the two extreme cases.

targets.target: Blocks and intermediate fields: an order anti-isomorphism between blocks containing α and intermediate fields of F(α)/F, with both maps explicit and the two ends confirmed
targets.note: Exactly as specified: an OrderIso built from Mathlib's block-stabilizer isomorphism and the Galois correspondence, with the inverse given as the roots of minpoly E α and both endpoint checks ({α} ↔ F(α), whole root set ↔ F) proved.

targets.target: Primitivity and intermediate fields: for 1 < natDegree p, preprimitive iff adjoin F {α} is an atom; prime degree implies primitive
targets.note: With the degree hypothesis the layer insists on, and the prime-degree corollary.

targets.target: 2-transitivity iff p/(X − α) is irreducible over F(α)
targets.note: The single declaration of the file, stated as an iff for 1 < natDegree p.

targets.target: Products and towers: Gal(pq) as the fibre product of Gal p × Gal q over the intersection of splitting fields, with the degenerate isomorphism case
targets.note: The image of restrictProd is characterized as the agreeing pairs, and surjectivity is proved equivalent to the intersection of the two splitting fields being ⊥ — the exact hypothesis the layer asks be carried. The equivariant-surjection remark for resolvents is not separately stated, but it is the restrictDvd_surjective the layer cites.

targets.target: Reducible polynomials: the stabilizer and block statements made per orbit / per irreducible factor
targets.note: Layer 0's orbit statement is the whole content of this item, and the layer's rule that nothing quantifies over 'the' root of a reducible polynomial is respected throughout the files.

duplicates.note: Its milestone 7.1 packages the order-reversing equivalence between IntermediateField ℚ K and the subgroups of Gal(M/ℚ) containing the fixing subgroup of K. That is the Galois side of this layer's stabilizer and intermediate-field dictionary, with the stabilizer of a root as the fixing subgroup, for number fields.

targets.target: The root-product formula: for monic f of degree n splitting in L, discr f = ∏_{i<j} (rᵢ − rⱼ)²
targets.note: Fills Mathlib's own TODO in Resultant/Basic.lean; Mathlib defines discr through the resultant with the derivative but proves no product form.

targets.target: The consequences: discr (f*g) with its resultant cross term, base change along a ring morphism, and discr ≠ 0 ↔ Separable over a field and over a domain
targets.note: Both separability readings are proved, and the ℤ → ZMod p specialization Layer 5 needs is stated as its own lemma.

targets.target: The ⚠ pinning the field hypothesis: over ℤ, X² − 1 has discr 4 ≠ 0 and is not Separable
targets.note: The exact regression witness the layer names, as two theorems.

targets.target: The comparison lemmas: Cubic.discr = (toPoly).discr, and Algebra.discr of a power basis = (minpoly).discr
targets.note: Both consistency lemmas between the three discriminant APIs, exactly as listed.

targets.target: The square root δ = ∏_{i<j}(rᵢ − rⱼ) with σ δ = sign(σ)·δ, and the discriminant test IsSquare (discr f) ↔ image ≤ alternatingGroup
targets.note: The equivariance σ δ = sign · δ is AlgEquiv.map_discrSqrt, the test carries ringChar F ≠ 2, and isSquare_discr_of_char_two is the named witness that the characteristic hypothesis cannot be dropped.

targets.target: The discriminant quadratic extension F(√disc f) with its API: characterization, fixed field of the even part, functoriality, edge cases
targets.note: Built: discrField as the adjunction of the square roots of discr f (a splitting field of X² − C (discr f) when one exists), trivial exactly when the discriminant is a square, of degree 2 otherwise, Galois away from characteristic 2, and the comparison theorem fixedField_evenAutSubgroup. discrField_map is naturality in the ambient extension E (along E ≃ₐ[F] E′). Missing: the functoriality the layer asks for in the base field, meaning invariance under an isomorphism of base fields and base change along F → F′ when the discriminant stays a nonsquare.

targets.target: Worked instances as acceptance tests: the quadratic case, x³ − 3x − 1 with discr 81 a square, x³ − 2 with discr −108 not
targets.note: No declaration in the baseline computes the discriminant of x³ − 3x − 1 or x³ − 2, or states the corresponding alternating-group membership; grep for those polynomials in both libraries finds nothing. These are acceptance tests rather than theory, so the layer stands otherwise complete.

duplicates.note: Its milestone 3.2 proves Algebra.discr of the power basis of an integral primitive element equal to Polynomial.discr (minpoly ℤ θ), noting that Mathlib never connects the two. That is the number-field case of this layer's comparison lemma, which Tau Ceti has in general as Algebra.discr_powerBasis_eq_minpoly_discr.

targets.target: ResolventSpec n: a subgroup H, an invariant Φ, an exact-stabilizer proof, and the integral symmetric orbit product; with its constructors, naturality and uniqueness API
targets.note: Missing: the bundled structure and every registered specification. The fourth field's content is there — existsUnique_orbitProduct proves that the integral symmetric expression exists and is unique, via esymmSubst_injective — and the rename-orbit naturality is there, but there is no ResolventSpec type, no exact-stabilizer theorem for any invariant, and no D₄, F₂₀ or pair-sum instance.

targets.target: The symmetric-polynomial descent in five milestones: invariance, symmetry of coefficients, the fundamental theorem, Vieta, agreement
targets.note: All five steps are present: rename-invariance of the universal resolvent, symmetry of each coefficient, the integral descent through Mathlib's fundamental theorem, and the agreement of the coefficient-side and root-side objects at a root enumeration of a monic polynomial.

targets.target: Specialization at a polynomial over any coefficient ring, with base change, coefficient integrality, reduction mod p, degree and monicity
targets.note: vietaHom is the specialization the layer calls ResolventSpec.specialize, with base change (vietaHom_map), monicity and degree over every ring. Missing here: the closed forms, since no specification is registered to specialize.

targets.target: The orbit resolvent galResolvent Φ x, with its degree, independence of numbering, and comparison with the universal object
targets.note: Built as specified, with the orbit taken over ℤ and the values the images of the integral renamings — the ⚠ the layer attaches to this item.

targets.target: Root data: a root enumeration forces splitting, and is injective iff the mapped polynomial is separable
targets.note: Mathlib supplies the content: splits ↔ card roots = natDegree (Polynomial.splits_iff_card_roots), and for a nonzero split polynomial, roots nodup ↔ separable (Polynomial.nodup_roots_iff_of_splits, and nodup_aroots_iff_of_splits for the mapped polynomial). Missing: the two milestones stated for a root enumeration x : Fin n → L, splitting from a full enumeration and injectivity of x ↔ separability. The agreement theorem map_vietaHom_eq_galResolvent_of_roots takes such an enumeration as a hypothesis.

targets.target: The factorization theorem: under separability of the specialized resolvent, the irreducible factors correspond to the Galois orbits on Sₙ/H, with the rational-root corollary
targets.note: Nothing in either library states this. It is the central theorem of the layer and everything downstream (the quartic table, the quintic criterion, the certificates) depends on it.

targets.target: The degenerate case in both directions, with the x⁵ − x collision witness (resolvent sextic (X − 2)⁴(X² + 16))
targets.note: Absent; no declaration mentions x⁵ − x as a resolvent-collision witness.

targets.target: Tschirnhaus transforms: tschirnhausPolynomial, TschirnhausAdmissible, and the transport of the subgroup bound
targets.note: Absent from both libraries; grep for 'tschirnhaus' in either baseline finds nothing.

targets.target: The quartic: valid depression, the D₄ invariant x₀x₂ + x₁x₃, resolventCubic = X³ − pX² − 4rX + (4pr − q²), discr agreement, and the four-row decision table
targets.note: Absent. There is no resolventCubic, no proof that a separable quartic has a separable resolvent cubic, and no row of the decision table.

targets.target: The quintic: Dummit's F₂₀ invariant, resolventSextic, the acceptance identity against formula (2′), and the solvability criterion
targets.note: Absent. No F₂₀ invariant, no resolventSextic, and no statement relating IsSolvable f.Gal to conjugacy into F₂₀ or to a rational root of the sextic.

targets.target: Linear resolvents: the pair-sum invariant x₀ + x₁ for a quintic, with stabilizer of order 12 and an orbit of exactly ten elements
targets.note: Absent; the general orbit machinery would support it but no instance is registered.

targets.target: factorDegrees f p with its API: constructor, multiplicity, sum, the irreducibility comparison, examples
targets.note: Defined through normalizedFactors as specified, with fifteen API lemmas and exactly the two worked examples the layer names: factorDegrees (X⁵ − X − 1) 2 = {3,2} and at 5 = {5}.

targets.target: The multiplicity-one comparison when p ∤ discr f, from the base change of discr
targets.note: The separability half is exactly the one-line consequence of Layer 3 the layer describes; the multiset-of-distinct-degrees restatement is not separately named.

targets.target: IsGoodPrime f p (p ∤ disc f) and ResolventSpec.IsGoodPrime spec f p (the conjunction with p ∤ disc of the specialized resolvent)
targets.note: Neither predicate exists; grep for IsGoodPrime / goodPrime in both libraries finds nothing. The second is not definable yet anyway, since Layer 4 registers no specification.

targets.target: Factor degrees are Frobenius orbit sizes, for a squarefree monic polynomial over a finite field
targets.note: Proved over a finite field with no Galois theory over ℚ, as the layer requires — the orbit of the Frobenius on the roots of an irreducible factor has cardinality its degree.

targets.target: Dedekind's factorization theorem, imported: some σ ∈ Gal has fullCycleType equal to factorDegrees f p when p ∤ discr f
targets.note: Not in the baseline under exists_gal_fullCycleType_eq_factorizationType or any variant; the supplier roadmap (NumberFieldArithmetic Layer 3) has not landed it, so the abbreviated restatement this layer owns cannot exist yet either. Tau Ceti's KummerDedekind file has the ramification-index and inertia-degree half but not the Frobenius cycle-type statement.

targets.target: The membership statement and its consequences: factorDegrees ∈ the set of fullCycleTypes of the image; irreducible mod p implies irreducible over ℚ; (1,…,1,2) in prime degree gives S_p; (1,…,1,3) with primitivity gives Aₙ
targets.note: Absent, because it is the imported theorem restated. The recognition inputs it feeds (Layer 1) exist, and Mathlib's irreducible_of_irreducible_map gives the mod-p irreducibility criterion directly without the Galois route, but the membership statement and the three named consequences are not declared.

targets.target: What factorization types do and do not give (lower bounds on the order, no containment in a proper subgroup)
targets.note: A scoping remark with no declaration behind it; nothing in the baseline states the D₅-against-A₅ illustration.

duplicates.note: Owns Dedekind's theorem itself (exists_gal_fullCycleType_eq_factorizationType and factorizationType_eq_cycleType_isArithFrobAt); this layer imports the statement rather than proving it, so the overlap is a declared supplier contract, not a duplication.

targets.target: The label API: numTransitiveGroups, TransitiveGroupIndex, referenceSubgroup with one theorem per row of the nT j table, TransitiveGroupLabel
targets.note: All four definitions exist with numTransitiveGroups = 1,1,2,5,5 and a simp lemma per row giving the generators; label membership is conjugacy of the image to a reference subgroup, as specified.

targets.target: Basic properties and naturality: every reference subgroup is transitive; the label is conjugation- and transport-invariant
targets.note: Transitivity of every reference subgroup is proved once and transported to any labelled group, as the layer plans.

targets.target: Comparison lemmas: a label forces equal order, parity, primitivity and solvability, and each row is identified with a familiar group (e.g. referenceSubgroup 4 2 ≃* DihedralGroup 4)
targets.note: Only the two rows that are alternatingGroup and ⊤ are identified with named groups; there is no MulEquiv with DihedralGroup 4 or any cyclic/Klein/Frobenius group, and no theorem deriving equal order, parity, primitivity or solvability from a label. Only transitivity is transported.

targets.target: HasGaloisLabel f j, with independence of the numbering and the transport of the invariants to f.Gal
targets.note: Not defined anywhere in the baseline; the predicate is the bridge from the group-side label to a statement about a polynomial, and everything in the rest of the layer is phrased in terms of it.

targets.target: The classification theorems: for each n ≤ 5, every transitive subgroup of Perm (Fin n) is conjugate to exactly one referenceSubgroup n j, with the named chain of steps in each degree
targets.note: Absent. The reference subgroups are defined but no existence or disjointness theorem is proved, so the label is not yet known to be well defined on transitive subgroups. This is the load-bearing content of the layer.

targets.target: Order recognizes the label in low degree, and the degree-5 recognition theorems (element of order 6 gives S₅; even parity with an element of order 3 gives A₅)
targets.note: Absent, and blocked by the classification above.

targets.target: Solvability and the labels in degree 5: an irreducible quintic is solvable iff its label is 5T1, 5T2 or 5T3
targets.note: Absent; needs both the degree-5 classification and the Layer 4 sextic criterion, neither of which exists.

targets.target: Classification from the discriminant and the resolvents: the degree-3, degree-4 and four degree-5 named theorems, plus the regression theorem discriminant_and_sextic_do_not_distinguish_C5_D5
targets.note: Absent. The discriminant inputs exist (Layer 3) but the resolvent inputs do not (Layer 4), so none of these can be stated yet.

targets.target: QuinticCertificate with Verifies, check, and the soundness theorem cert.check f = true → HasGaloisLabel f cert.label
targets.note: Absent; no certificate structure of any kind for Galois labels exists in the baseline.

duplicates.note: Defines passport membership by the same conjugacy spelling and says so explicitly ('exactly as PolynomialGaloisGroups spells label membership'), and needs the same reference-subgroup and transitive-group data for monodromy groups.

Builds a different LMFDB label (the number-field prefix d.r.D), and explicitly disclaims the database-ordering coordinate; the overlap is only in the shared caution about what an LMFDB label certifies.

targets.target: HasFullSymmetricGaloisGroup f: separability plus surjectivity of galActionHom, with the X^n regression test
targets.note: The predicate does not exist. Mathlib has the injectivity of galActionHom and, for an irreducible rational polynomial of prime degree with exactly two non-real roots, its bijectivity — which is a sufficient condition for one family, not the predicate.

targets.target: The theorem: for every n ≥ 1 an explicit monic f : ℤ[X] of degree n, irreducible over ℚ, with full symmetric Galois action
targets.note: Absent from both libraries. Mathlib has the prime-degree solvability application (Abel–Ruffini) but nothing realizing Sₙ for general n.

targets.target: Milestone 1: a monic irreducible polynomial of each degree d ≥ 1 over ZMod 2
targets.note: Only the degrees 2 and 3 instances exist, as one-off examples in the FactorDegrees file. No general existence statement over ZMod 2 (or over a finite field) is in the baseline under a searchable name.

targets.target: Milestones 2 and 3: squarefree monic polynomials over ZMod 3 with factor degrees (1, n−1), and over ZMod 5 with exactly one quadratic factor and all other degrees odd
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Milestone 4: a coefficientwise Chinese remainder theorem realizing prescribed monic reductions at 2, 3 and 5 by one monic integral polynomial
targets.note: Mathlib has the scalar CRT the layer cites, but nothing lifts it coefficientwise to monic polynomials of a fixed degree.

targets.target: Milestones 5 to 8: admissibility of 2, 3, 5 from base change of discr; irreducibility mod 2; the four group-theoretic steps; the small-n cases
targets.note: The prerequisites this layer imports from Layers 1, 3 and 5 are in place — the base change of discr, three of the four group-theoretic steps (the fourth, an n-cycle gives transitivity, is immediate from Mathlib's cycle API), and the irreducibility criterion. What is missing is everything this layer itself owns: the finite-field constructions, the CRT lift and the assembly.

targets.target: The alternating examples: x³ − 3x − 1 for 3T1, x⁴ + 8x + 12 for 4T4, x⁵ + 20x − 16 for 5T4
targets.note: None of the three polynomials appears in either library, and the label predicate they would be stated with (HasGaloisLabel, Layer 6) does not exist.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/QuadraticFormInva.summary: The bottom of the roadmap is largely built and the top is not. Tau Ceti already has most of Layer 1 (hyperbolic plane, Witt decomposition for regular forms, Witt cancellation, reflections, Cartan–Dieudonné, Witt's extension theorem; missing are the decomposition of degenerate forms, Lam I.4.4 and the monotonicity of the Witt index under base change), almost all of Layer 0 (the square-class group with its multiplicative avatar and finiteness, Represents / unitValueSet with the representation criterion, the binary normal forms, the chain relation with Witt's chain-equivalence theorem, and RegularFormClass as the quotient), and the discriminant half of Layer 3 (discr, signedDiscr, the sum/product/scaling formulas, base change; not yet the Gram-determinant description), plus a substantial Layer 2 (quaternion norm form and pure norm form, Nrd multiplicativity, and the split cases (1,b), (a,−a), (a,b²) and the Steinberg relation as explicit AlgEquivs onto M₂(K)). Everything above that is absent: no Witt ring and no fundamental ideal, no Pfister forms, no quaternion symbol in Br(K), no Hasse or Clifford invariant, no Hilbert symbol, no quadratic defect, no local classification, no comparison of H²(G_K, μ₂) with the Brauer group, no cup-norm theorem, no Stiefel–Whitney classes and no Scharlau transfer — grep over both baselines for hasseInvariant, hilbertSymbol, wittRing, fundamentalIdeal, pfister, quadraticDefect and stiefelWhitney finds nothing. The substrates those layers consume are partly in place (Tau Ceti's BrauerGroup with its CommGroup structure and base change, the CentralSimple directory, the local-field normalized valuation, unit filtration, graded pieces and Teichmüller lift, the injective Kummer map into H¹ but not the Kummer isomorphism, since Hilbert 90 for G_K is missing, a low-degree continuous cup product and corestriction for an abstract open subgroup, Mathlib's Valuation.IsUniformizer, the odd-residue case of the local square theorem, and central simplicity of the Clifford algebra of a split even-dimensional form), so the missing work is the quadratic-form content itself rather than its foundations. One correction to the roadmap's own framing: Layer 2's centrality input is not entirely missing — TauCeti.Quaternion.instIsCentral proves ℍ[R] central, though only for the standard structure constants and not for ℍ[K,a,b].

targets.target: Square-class interop: the multiplicative avatar Kˣ/(Kˣ)², the ZMod 2-module dictionary, pushforward along a field map, finiteness through Nat.card
targets.note: All four bullets: the additive ZMod 2-module SquareClassGroup, the multiplicative quotient, the equivalence between them, pushforward along a RingHom with its id/comp laws, and the finiteness transfer through Nat.card that Layer 6 was to consume.

targets.target: Represents and unitValueSet, with Represents Q 0 for every Q and closure under squares
targets.note: Exactly the conventions the layer fixes, including represents_zero stated with no hypothesis and kept separate from anisotropy (Equivalent.anisotropic_iff is in the same file).

targets.target: The representation criterion (Lam I.2.3, I.3.5): for regular Q and a : Kˣ, a ∈ unitValueSet Q iff Q ⊥ ⟨−a⟩ is isotropic
targets.note: Stated for units only, as the layer insists, and in both the Nondegenerate and the radical-trivial hypothesis shapes.

targets.target: Binary forms in normal form: c ∈ unitValueSet ⟨a,b⟩ ↔ ⟨a,b⟩ ≅ ⟨c, abc⟩, and the binary equivalence criterion (Lam I.5.1)
targets.note: Both spellings of the second coefficient (abc and its inverse form) and the two halves of the Lam I.5.1 criterion are proved.

targets.target: Chain equivalence: PermutationStep, BinaryStep, DiagonalStep, DiagonalChain, the containment of permutations in binary steps, and Witt's chain-equivalence theorem
targets.note: The four relations under exactly the roadmap's names, with the hard direction (Lam I.5.2) proved and the rank-0 and rank-1 edge cases separated out.

targets.target: RegularFormPresentation, regularFormSetoid, RegularFormClass, and the quotient map
targets.note: Including the functoriality bullet: presentations and classes push forward along K →+* L, and rank and discr commute with it (RegularFormClass.rank_baseChange, discr_baseChange).

targets.target: The descent principle: a PermutationStep- and BinaryStep-invariant function on diagonal tuples descends uniquely to RegularFormClass
targets.note: Missing as a named declaration. The two ingredients are there and the existing invariants (discr, signedDiscr) are each descended by an ad hoc argument, which is exactly what the layer says should be stated once and reused; no general lift out of regularFormSetoid exists.

targets.target: The comparison with Serre IV Thm 5 on contiguous orthogonal bases
targets.note: Nothing in either library defines contiguity of orthogonal bases; grep for 'contiguous' over both baselines finds nothing.

tauceti:Completed/ContourIntegration.summary: Everything this completed roadmap asks for is built, sorry-free, in Tau Ceti under TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/ (123 files, about 1150 declarations, no sorry or axiom). That covers: piecewise-C¹ curves, immersions and ℤ-cycles; the PV-defined generalized winding number with integrality, homotopy invariance and vanishing on the unbounded component; the model sector and HW Props 2.2 and 2.3; residues via meromorphicOrderAt, polar-part decompositions, the circle and null-homologous classical residue theorems and the argument principle; the homology Cauchy theorem and integral formula by Dixon's argument, for curves and cycles; and HW Thm 3.3 with conditions (A′)/(B), in single-curve and cycle forms, plus the half-residue case, a simple-pole unconditional form, real-axis PV applications and the Dirichlet integral. Mathlib contributes only ingredients (circle/disc/annulus/rectangle Cauchy theory, the circle Cauchy integral formula, curve integrals with C²-homotopy invariance, meromorphicOrderAt, logDeriv). It has no winding number, principal value, residue, principal-part/Laurent-coefficient API (the README wrongly credits Mathlib with principal-part machinery), residue theorem, argument principle or homology Cauchy theorem. Genuinely missing, and outside the pinned scope: HW Thm 3.3 for accumulation-free singular sets and essential singularities (the residue is only meaningful at meromorphic points), cycle-level versions of Props 2.2/2.3, a cyclic re-basing lemma to remove the basepoint-off-singularity hypotheses, and a signed-curvature API.

targets.note: Additivity requires MeromorphicAt of the summands (necessarily); scaling is unconditional. No sorry.

targets.note: f meromorphic at z₀ with meromorphicOrderAt f z₀ = n ∈ ℤ gives residue (logDeriv f) z₀ = n. targets.note: Single closed piecewise-C¹ curve and genuine ℤ-cycles, with null-homology imposed on the whole cycle (cancellation between generators allowed). targets.note: A piecewise-C¹ loop with a continuous Path.Homotopy to the constant path inside Ω is null-homologous in Ω (one direction only). No sorry.

targets.target: Dixon's argument: g(w,z) = (f(w)−f(z))/(w−z) glues to an entire function that vanishes by Liouville
targets.note: dixonH1/dixonH2/dixonFunction are irreducible_def definitions (no axioms); the glued function is entire and tends to 0 at infinity, hence 0. The theorem is named the homology Cauchy theorem and Dixon's proof is attributed, as the layer asks. No sorry.

targets.target: HW Thm 3.3 (pinned form): U open, S ⊆ U finite, f holomorphic on U ∖ S and meromorphic on S, C a null-homologous closed piecewise-C¹ immersion in U (basepoint off S) ⇒ PV (2πi)⁻¹∮_C f = Σ_s n_s(C) Res_s f

targets.note: (A′): each s ∈ S is met finitely often, and at an interior or basepoint crossing of a pole of order n the curve is flat of order n (HW Def 3.2, perpendicular distance to a one-sided tangent line). (B): at every order > 1 on-curve pole the crossing (or basepoint) angle is a rational multiple of π, and k·θ ∈ 2πℤ for each nonzero higher Laurent coefficient. tauceti:Completed/OrthogonalL2Bases.summary: Every target of this completed roadmap is in Tau Ceti, sorry-free: the Hermite polynomial API (derivative recursion, Gaussian-weight integrability, the one-step pairing recursion, the generating function, and both orthogonality normalizations), the Hermite functions ψₙ with their regularity, SchwartzMap packaging, parity, ladder relations, creation/annihilation/number/oscillator CLMs and the eigen-equation, hermiteHilbertBasis with coe_hermiteHilbertBasis and Parseval, the Fourier-eigenfunction relation on the 2π-scaled functions, the Gaussian measure-side basis with the dilation lemma, the family-agnostic spine (moment determinacy in Probability/Moments, weightL2Isometry, HilbertBasis.mapₗᵢ, hilbertBasisOfWeightedMeasure / hilbertBasisOfOrthogonalSystem, prodHilbertBasis and piHilbertBasis), the Chebyshev instance with its cosine transfer, and both multidimensional Hermite bases. Mathlib contributes the Hermite polynomials themselves (Polynomial.hermite, degree_hermite, the Rodrigues formula), the Chebyshev polynomials with measureT and its orthogonality relations, HilbertBasis.mkOfOrthogonalEqBot, and the Fourier-integral machinery behind the Fourier-eigenfunction relation, plus the complexMGF/charFun and signed-measure (withDensityᵥ) API that the moment-determinacy engine runs on — and, as the roadmap claims, nothing else: no Hermite functions, no weight-to-measure L² isometry, no ≃ₗᵢ-transport of a HilbertBasis, and OrthonormalBasis.tensorProduct is Fintype-indexed and abstract, so it does not give the L²(μ ⊗ ν) statement B3 proves. Nothing on this roadmap is genuinely missing; the three open targets Part C names — IsFiniteMeasure measureT, the compactly supported instance of B1's moment lemma, and the real→RCLike cast of Chebyshev completeness — are all discharged in the baseline.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ConformalMapping.summary: This roadmap is essentially already built — not in Mathlib, but in Tau Ceti's own TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Conformal/ (about 110 files, ~2600 declarations, no sorry and no axiom). Every L0–L4 summit exists as a named theorem: TauCeti.rouche, TauCeti.hurwitz, TauCeti.morera, TauCeti.localDegree, TauCeti.montel, TauCeti.vitali, the Schwarz–Pick/pseudo-hyperbolic and Poincaré-metric API with the full classification of Aut(𝔻) (TauCeti.unitDiscAut, TauCeti.mem_unitDiscAut_iff), TauCeti.riemannMapping with its normalized and uniqueness companions, and the reflection/Painlevé/monodromy package (TauCeti.exists_differentiableOn_eqOn_conj_of_symmetric, TauCeti.monodromy_theorem), including reflection across an analytic arc and across a circle. Mathlib still supplies only the Cauchy foundations the README credits it with — the open mapping theorem, AbsMax, Schwarz's lemma, BranchLogRoot, plus Complex.exists_injective_not_dense_image_deriv_ne_zero in RiemannMapping.lean — and MontelSpace remains the unrelated locally-convex notion. What is genuinely unfinished is at the top: L5 has Carathéodory's continuity theorem but not the closure homeomorphism (injectivity of the boundary extension on the circle is never established, only the reduction TauCeti.injOn_closure_of_injOn_frontier and the packaging TauCeti.closureHomeomorph), and L6 has the whole Schwarz–Christoffel apparatus — integrand, primitive, vertices, edges, the vertex at infinity, the polygon and its Jordan boundary — but not the statement that the map is a bijection of ℍ onto the polygon's interior, which SchwarzChristoffel/Infinity.lean explicitly leaves to later work.

targets.target: Rouché's theorem (symmetric and classical forms; zeros counted with multiplicity)
targets.note: Disc form: f, g analyticOnNhd on closedBall c R with ‖f − g‖ < ‖f‖ on the sphere gives equality of the finsums of analyticOrderNatAt over ball c R. The symmetric hypothesis ‖f − g‖ < ‖f‖ + ‖g‖ and a null-homologous cycle version over an arbitrary open set are also proved. Mathlib has no Rouché theorem at all.

targets.target: Hurwitz: a locally uniform limit of zero-free holomorphic maps is zero-free or identically zero; the injectivity corollary
targets.note: Stated for TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn on a connected open set, with the zero-counting input taken from the argument principle; hurwitz_injOn is the limit-of-injections dichotomy the Riemann mapping theorem needs. Mathlib's only Hurwitz-type lemmas are private inside mathlib4#33505, not in the pinned baseline.

targets.target: Morera's theorem as a named theorem
targets.note: TauCeti.morera is a two-line specialization of Mathlib's conservativity ↔ differentiability equivalence, which is the stronger statement; the layer's target is precisely to expose it under the classical name, and it does.

targets.target: The open-mapping degree: local valence of a holomorphic map, and the local injectivity criterion
targets.note: Every nearby value is attained exactly analyticOrderNatAt-many times, counted with multiplicity and (for a simple value) as a cardinality; the derivative of a holomorphic injection of an open set vanishes nowhere. Mathlib has the open mapping theorem but no degree/valence count.

targets.target: The consumed inputs: argument principle, residues, winding numbers, homological Cauchy theorem (from the ContourIntegration roadmap), open mapping and maximum modulus (from Mathlib)
targets.note: The layer says consume, do not re-derive, and that is what happens: the ArgumentPrinciple.lean file here is a thin disc-shaped restatement over the Contour development, and the open-mapping/AbsMax inputs come straight from Mathlib.

duplicates.note: Owns the argument principle, residues and winding numbers that L0 declares it consumes; the overlap is by design and L0 adds only the conformal-geometric consequences.

targets.target: Local boundedness of a family of holomorphic maps, with its equicontinuity consequences
targets.note: Bounded on each compact subset, exactly as the generality bar asks; the Cauchy estimate on a doubled ball gives local Lipschitz bounds, hence equicontinuity of the family and of its derivatives.

targets.target: Montel's selection theorem: locally bounded ⇒ every sequence has a locally uniformly convergent subsequence with holomorphic limit
targets.note: Stated not just for ℂ but for maps into any proper complex normed space E, with the precompactness of the restricted family in C(Ω,E) as an iff; the roadmap only asked for the scalar case. Mathlib's MontelSpace (Analysis/LocallyConvex/Montel.lean) is the unrelated locally-convex notion, as the README says, and is not used.

targets.target: Vitali's theorem: a locally bounded family converging pointwise on a set with a limit point converges locally uniformly
targets.note: Proved by Montel plus the identity theorem on subsequential limits; no Vitali theorem for holomorphic families exists in Mathlib (Mathlib's 'Vitali' names are the covering-family and Vitali–Carathéodory results in measure theory).

targets.target: The pseudo-hyperbolic metric on 𝔻 and the Schwarz–Pick inequality for holomorphic self-maps
targets.note: |(f z − f w)/(1 − conj (f w)·f z)| ≤ |(z − w)/(1 − conj w·z)| for a holomorphic self-map of the ball, obtained by conjugating Mathlib's Schwarz lemma with the disc automorphisms; the triangle inequality for the pseudo-hyperbolic expression is proved separately.

targets.target: The derivative form of Schwarz–Pick, and the rigidity/equality case
targets.note: Equality anywhere forces the map to be a disc automorphism — the rigidity half the Riemann mapping proof's maximizer argument relies on. Mathlib has only the derivative bound at the centre (Complex.norm_deriv_le_div_of_mapsTo_ball).

targets.target: The hyperbolic (Poincaré) metric on 𝔻: distance, geodesics, length, the metric-space instance
targets.note: A full MetricSpace instance on the type synonym PoincareDisc with the closed forms (cosh/sinh/tanh/exp of the distance), the geodesic and orthogonal-circle theory, and Schwarz–Pick as 1-Lipschitzness — well beyond what the layer asks for. Mathlib has the hyperbolic metric only on the upper half-plane (UpperHalfPlane.dist).

targets.target: The disc automorphism group Aut(𝔻) = {e^{iθ}(z−a)/(1−ā z)}
targets.note: A genuine Subgroup of Equiv.Perm Complex.UnitDisc, with membership characterized as being one of the standard automorphisms, a unique (u, a) ∈ Circle × UnitDisc parametrization, transitivity, and the rotation stabilizer of 0. Mathlib has Complex.UnitDisc but no automorphism group.

duplicates.note: Also develops hyperbolic geodesics, half-planes and convex polygons, but on Mathlib's upper half-plane rather than on 𝔻, and for Fuchsian-group purposes; the metric content overlaps, the Schwarz–Pick and Aut(𝔻) content does not.

targets.target: The Riemann mapping theorem: a simply connected open Ω ⊊ ℂ admits a holomorphic bijection onto the unit disc
targets.note: Stated exactly in the shape the generality bar prescribes: IsOpen Ω, IsSimplyConnected Ω (Mathlib's SimplyConnectedSpace ↥Ω, which carries nonemptiness), Ω ≠ univ, conclusion BijOn f Ω (ball 0 1) with DifferentiableOn and nonvanishing derivative. Sorry-free. Mathlib's RiemannMapping.lean holds only the two partial results cited, which are strictly weaker.

targets.target: The biholomorphism packaging: holomorphic inverse, partial homeomorphism, homeomorphism of Ω with the disc
targets.note: The packaged ≃ / ConformalAt companions the layer asks for, including the two-simply-connected-domains form and the ConformalAt statement in Conformal.lean.

targets.target: The extremal-family argument: the pointed injection family is nonempty and normal, and |f′(z₀)| attains its maximum
targets.note: Exactly the standard route the layer prescribes — Montel + Hurwitz give the maximizer, and the Koebe square-root trick shows a non-surjective maximizer can be beaten.

targets.target: Uniqueness up to Aut(𝔻), and the normalized Riemann map
targets.note: Two Riemann maps differ by composition with a standard disc automorphism, and the normalization f z₀ = 0, deriv f z₀ > 0 pins the map uniquely — more than the layer's 'uniqueness up to Aut(𝔻)'.

targets.target: The square-root / holomorphic-log step, consumed from Mathlib's BranchLogRoot
targets.note: Mathlib supplies continuous branches of log and n-th roots on a simply connected open set; TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/BranchLogRoot.lean upgrades the log branch to a holomorphic one and derives holomorphic n-th roots from it, and DiscInjection.lean's square-root trick uses that, exactly as the layer directs.

targets.target: Schwarz reflection across ℝ, with the explicit witness F z = if 0 ≤ z.im then f z else conj (f (conj z))
targets.note: Hypotheses are exactly the classical ones: Ω open and conj-stable, f continuous on Ω ∩ {0 ≤ im}, holomorphic on Ω ∩ {0 < im}, real on the axis. Sorry-free; the antiholomorphic-composition lemma the layer calls L4.0 is inside Reflection/Basic.lean. Absent from Mathlib.

targets.target: Reflection across an analytic arc and across a circle, by Möbius reduction
targets.note: The arc case is run through an analytic chart carrying the arc to the real locus; the circle case through the Möbius map of Reflection/Circle/Conjugate.lean. Injectivity of the reflected map is proved too, which the layer does not ask for.

targets.target: Painlevé removability across an arc (and across a line or a circle)
targets.note: The Morera/rectangle argument is carried in Removability/Basic.lean and transported to any subset of a line, to a charted analytic arc, and to a sphere. Distinct from Mathlib's point-removability (Complex.differentiableOn_update_limUnder_insert_of_isLittleO), which removes isolated points only.

targets.target: The monodromy theorem: continuations along homotopic paths agree
targets.note: Analytic continuation along a path is defined for germs of maps ℂ → E into a complex Banach space, and the monodromy theorem is proved both rel endpoints and for a free homotopy with moving endpoints. Mathlib's monodromy theorem is the abstract lifting statement for a separated local homeomorphism, not the analytic one; TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/HolomorphicSheaf.lean supplies the étale space that would connect them.

duplicates.note: Names Schwarz reflection as the tool for boundary regularity under totally real boundary conditions — a consumer of L4, not a second construction of it.
Explicitly disclaims duplication ('No Schwarz reflection, boundary correspondence, or universal-cover argument is duplicated'), so it consumes L4/L5 rather than restating them.

targets.target: Carathéodory's continuity theorem: a conformal map of the disc onto a bounded Jordan domain extends continuously to the closed disc
targets.note: Proved in full by the crosscut/length–area argument, with the Jordan-curve and crosscut machinery (Crosscut/*.lean, Jordan/*.lean, ClusterSet.lean, LengthArea.lean) built out underneath it. Sorry-free.

targets.target: The boundary correspondence: the extension carries frontier to frontier, and is a homeomorphism of the closures
targets.note: Missing: injectivity of the continuous extension on the bounding circle. closureHomeomorph takes that injectivity as a hypothesis, and injOn_closure_of_injOn_frontier reduces closed-disc injectivity to it, but no theorem in the baseline discharges it for a Jordan domain — so the milestone's 'homeomorphism of the closures' is proved only conditionally. Caratheodory.lean states this gap itself.

targets.target: Prime ends (explicitly out of scope for the L5 milestone)
targets.note: Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti defines prime ends; grep over both baselines for 'primeEnd'/'PrimeEnd' finds nothing. The layer scopes this out, so it does not hold the verdict back.

duplicates.note: Consumes the boundary correspondence for the analytic modular curve and explicitly disclaims duplicating it.

targets.target: The Schwarz–Christoffel integrand ∏ (z − aᵢ)^{eᵢ} and its primitive, holomorphic and conformal on ℍ
targets.note: The integrand is zero-free and holomorphic on the upper half-plane, the primitive is conformal there and characterized by its derivative and normalization. Nothing comparable exists in Mathlib.

targets.target: Boundary behaviour: the map extends to ℝ, the edges are straight segments, the prevertices map to vertices, the turning is by the exterior angles
targets.note: Each prevertex-free real interval goes to a straight segment, consecutive edge directions differ by π times the exponent, the two unbounded edges close up at a single vertex at infinity, and the vertices are affinely independent at convex prevertices.

targets.target: The image polygon, and that the map is a conformal bijection of ℍ onto its interior
targets.note: Missing: the summit itself. The polygon is constructed and its boundary is identified with the range of the compactified boundary map (a Jordan curve when that map is injective), but no theorem says the primitive is a bijection of ℍ onto the polygon's interior; SchwarzChristoffel/Infinity.lean:39 records that 'identifying the image of the half-plane with its interior, is left to later work'. That identification is what needs L5's boundary correspondence, which is itself only conditional.

targets.target: The converse direction: every polygon is the image of ℍ under such a map (the classical Schwarz–Christoffel theorem)
targets.note: Nothing in the baseline produces prevertices from a given polygon; the development runs only in the forward direction, from exponents and prevertices to an image.

corrections.target: Degree bookkeeping: rootSet has natDegree elements, the action is faithful, Nat.card p.Gal = Nat.card of the image
corrections.why: Nat.card p.Gal ∣ p.natDegree! is a corollary of the faithful action, not a more general form of the degree bookkeeping.

corrections.target: Conjugate fields: G/H in equivariant bijection with the roots and with the F-embeddings; conjugate subfields correspond to conjugates of H; their number is [G : N_G(H)]
corrections.why: The equivariance of the Galois correspondence under conjugation is proved in both libraries: Mathlib's IsGalois.map_fixingSubgroup gives (σE).fixingSubgroup = σ·E.fixingSubgroup·σ⁻¹, and Tau Ceti's Subgroup.fixedField_map_conj gives fixedField (σHσ⁻¹) = σ(fixedField H), for any extension. Mathlib's IntermediateField.algHomAdjoinIntegralEquiv is the bijection between F-embeddings of F(α) and roots of minpoly F α, and MulAction.orbitEquivQuotientStabilizer gives G/H ≃ orbit. The audit's grep found only Multiquadratic lemmas.

corrections.why: The audit's own note lists two missing items of this milestone: the primitivity theorem for the product action, and the comparison MulEquiv D ≀ᵣ Q ≃* (Q → D) ⋊ Q′. The dihedral example WreathProduct (ZMod 2) (Fin 2) is also missing. WreathProduct.lean mentions RegularWreathProduct only in its docstring. With parts of the milestone missing, the target is partial.

corrections.why: ProfiniteCohomology Layer 13 lists as its first milestone the permutation wreath product (X → D) ⋊ Q generalizing RegularWreathProduct, the object this layer also asks for.

corrections.why: Functoriality in the base field is missing. The layer asks that F(√disc f) be preserved by an isomorphism of base fields and commute with base change F → F′ when the discriminant stays a nonsquare. TauCeti.discrField_map is naturality in the ambient extension (ψ : E ≃ₐ[F] E′), not in F. No declaration in Discriminant/Field.lean, or anywhere else, changes the base field. The note's 'transport along a base-field isomorphism' misreads discrField_map.

corrections.target: (layer verdict)
corrections.why: One target is absent (the worked instances x³ − 3x − 1 and x³ − 2) and one is now partial (base-change functoriality of the discriminant field), so 'built' overstates the layer.

corrections.target: (layer duplicates)
corrections.why: NumberFieldArithmetic 3.2 asks for Algebra.discr (power basis) = Polynomial.discr (minpoly), the same comparison as this layer's discriminant-API consistency lemma.

corrections.target: Root data: a root enumeration forces splitting, and is injective iff the mapped polynomial is separable
corrections.why: Mathlib has both facts in general form. Polynomial.splits_iff_card_roots says a polynomial splits iff card roots = natDegree, so an enumeration of the roots by Fin natDegree forces splitting. Polynomial.nodup_roots_iff_of_splits and nodup_aroots_iff_of_splits say a nonzero split polynomial has no repeated roots iff it is separable, and injectivity of the enumeration is nodup of univ.val.map x. Only the enumeration-shaped statements are missing.

corrections.why: Two parts of the milestone are missing. (1) The decomposition of every form, degenerate ones included, as q_t ⊥ m×ℍ ⊥ q_a with q_t the zero form on the radical. corrections.now: cites the public TauCeti.QuadraticMap.reflection, reflection_mem_orthogonalGroup, reflection_apply_of_isOrtho, reflection_mul_self and exists_reflectionOrthogonal_list_prod_eq; library unchanged (tauceti)

review.notes: Reviewed all 239 targets of the 49 layers: the audit's 238 plus one milestone it omitted. Mechanical check: all 678 original citations resolve in the pinned index at the cited file and line. No cited declaration body contains sorry or admit, and at the pin Tau Ceti has no sorry token outside comments and declares no axiom. Every citation was then read in the Lean source and compared with the layer text. PolynomialGaloisGroups, QuadraticFormInvariants and ConformalMapping were read by the reviewer. ContourIntegration and OrthogonalL2Bases were checked target by target by two delegated read-only passes, and every issue they reported was re-verified at source by the reviewer before being applied. Result: 73 corrections, and after them 695 citations, all resolving at file and line, at most five per target, with 19 private citations removed or replaced. Presence claims that overstated the Lean, 7 now partial: PGG general wreath products (no product-action primitivity theorem or RegularWreathProduct comparison, as the audit's own note said); PGG discrField (naturality only in the ambient extension, no base-field functoriality); QFI Witt decomposition (regular forms only, no degenerate q_t summand, no Lam I.4.4, and no totally isotropic subspace notion in either library); QFI Witt-index functoriality (no monotonicity under base change); QFI discriminant (the Gram-determinant comparison was miscited as QuadraticMap.orthogonalDetSquareClass, the determinant of an orthogonal map mod squares; only the diagonal discr'_weightedSumSquares exists); QFI 7A Kummer (only the injective kummerClassMap: no kummerIso, hilbert90 or h2KummerToUnits); QFI 7A corestriction (abstract open-subgroup cor in degrees 0–2 only, no G_L ≤ G_K transfer). Verdicts: PGG Layer 3 and QFI Layer 1 are now 'partly built'. Absence claims contradicted by the libraries, 5 now partial: PGG conjugate fields (Mathlib IsGalois.map_fixingSubgroup, Tau Ceti Subgroup.fixedField_map_conj, IntermediateField.algHomAdjoinIntegralEquiv); PGG root enumerations (Polynomial.splits_iff_card_roots, nodup_roots_iff_of_splits); QFI Clifford invariant (Mathlib CliffordAlgebra.equivOfIsometry, and Tau Ceti central simplicity for polarized even-dimensional forms); QFI 6A uniformizer (Mathlib Valuation.IsUniformizer applies to a local field's valuation, contrary to the note); QFI 6A local square theorem (the e = 0 case, unitFiltration_one_le_range_powMonoidHom_of_isUnit). ConformalMapping's BranchLogRoot step is 'both', since the holomorphic root is Tau Ceti's exists_differentiableOn_pow_eq. Added target: QFI Layer 9 'which functional' (partial, Mathlib Algebra.trace_ne_zero and traceForm_nondegenerate). Citation fixes: QFI Cartan–Dieudonné now cites the public reflection API; CM derivative Schwarz–Pick is norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_le; QFI 9 trace form no longer cites the gl_n trace form. Fit labels were downgraded where hypotheses were extra or weaker: CI decomposition lemmas carry a basepoint hypothesis, and the CI FTC lemmas need differentiability at every interior point. Notes were corrected where they misstated Mathlib or the proof route: Mathlib's logDeriv order lemmas, its C² homotopy invariance and convex primitives; hermite_succ is not the three-term recurrence; the pairing recursion does not use Mathlib's Rodrigues formula; moment determinacy goes through withDensityᵥ, i.e. a signed-measure argument. Duplicates: all 36 original ids resolve, none is retired. Removed 8 entries in 4 layers that listed the layer's own sub-layers (QFI 6 → 6A/6C, QFI 7 → 7B, OL2B Part A → A1/A3, Part B → B1–B3).
